svg.title: RP2350 pacemaker: board and patient wiring
svg.desc: Schematic, updated with the ZL70102 radio, TPS22860 load switch, TPS3839 supervisor and TS5A3159 polarity switch: the RP2350 pacemaker controller connects to an ADXL362 activity sensor and an ADS1292R heart-sensing front end on a shared SPI0 bus, an MCP4822 pacing amplitude DAC and an RF430CL330H NFC telemetry tag on a shared SPI1 bus, a DRV5032 magnet sensor, two TS5A3166 pacing switches, an AT24C256C diagnostic EEPROM on I2C0, a lithium-iodine battery on ADC0, and a host on two UARTs. The ADS1292R inputs and the pacing switch outputs both land on the tip and ring conductors of the RA and RV leads, which run to the simulated heart. The accelerometer, the Hall switch and the NFC tag couple to the patient's body, the clinician's magnet and the programmer's wand without wires.
svg.text: GP28 low = ring, bipolar · high = can, unipolar
its magnet sets the same field
dot = joined; plain crossing = not joined
The ADS1292R reads tip minus ring on the RA lead, and tip minus the TS5A3159's COM on the RV lead: the ring (bipolar) or the can (unipolar). The same tip takes
the pacing pulse when its TS5A3166 closes. Purple dashed arrows carry no current. The wand carries its own magnet, so placing it also closes the Hall switch.
VBAT flags are the same net as the cell's terminal.
